title: Why Is AECOM (ACM) Stock Up +11.77% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/1sskz68rv62i1.png

# Key Takeaways

* Shares of AECOM ([ACM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ACM/)) jumped 11.77%, or $8.53, to $81.03 in mid-morning trading Tuesday, after touching $83.54 shortly after the open.
* The primary catalyst was a fiscal fourth-quarter earnings beat: adjusted EPS of $1.63 topped the $1.59 consensus, up 20% year over year.
* Secondary drivers included record fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.2%, a record $28 billion backlog, a 1.3x book-to-burn ratio, and a 10% dividend increase to $0.34 per quarter.
* Results were not flawless: revenue fell 7% to $3.88 billion and missed estimates, while GAAP fiscal 2027 EPS guidance landed below consensus.
* Peer engineering and construction names and infrastructure-focused funds were roughly flat, and the S&P 500 edged lower, confirming the move was company-specific rather than sector-driven.
* **News Significance Score: 63/100** — A solid earnings beat paired with an unusually large, roughly seven-times-normal price move.
* Traders are now watching whether the gap holds above the pre-earnings range and whether delivery of the second construction management project stays on schedule.

# Opening Summary

AECOM ([ACM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ACM/)) is a Fortune 500 infrastructure consulting firm that designs, engineers, and manages large public and private works — transportation networks, water systems, facilities, and environmental programs — generating about $15.1 billion in revenue in fiscal 2026. The stock closed Monday at $72.50 and was trading at $81.03 on Tuesday morning, a gain of $8.53, or 11.77%. The direction is clearly higher. The move followed the company's fiscal fourth-quarter report, released after Monday's close, which delivered an adjusted earnings beat, record margins, record backlog, and a larger dividend.

# Earnings Beat and Record Margins

Adjusted earnings per share rose 20% to $1.63, ahead of the $1.59 consensus, while GAAP earnings from continuing operations held at $0.99. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 9% to $358 million and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 170 basis points to a quarterly record of 19.2%. The adjusted operating margin also set a fourth-quarter record at 18.2%, up 110 basis points.

The quality of the beat mattered as much as the headline. Net service revenue — which strips out pass-through subcontractor costs and is the metric management steers the business by — rose 3% after adjusting for fewer working days, with design growth accelerating to 6%. The International segment posted a record 14.8% adjusted operating margin, up 270 basis points, helped by strength in the U.K., Australia, and a return to growth in the Middle East.

# Record Backlog and De-Risked Construction Projects

Total backlog rose 13% to a record $28 billion, supported by $13.4 billion of annual wins and a 1.3x book-to-burn ratio. Management also said the two troubled construction management projects that triggered a $337 million pretax charge earlier in the year remain on track with previously communicated timelines and budgets, with the first phase of one project substantially complete and the second project due near the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

That reassurance is central to the rally. The charge had pushed the company to a loss in the prior quarter and helped drive the shares to a 52-week low of $56.39 in early October. Removing the worst-case scenario from the CM overhang allowed investors to value the core design and advisory franchise again.

# Guidance, Dividend, and Analyst Reaction

Fiscal 2027 guidance came in at adjusted EPS of $6.15 to $6.35, a midpoint of $6.25 that sits marginally above consensus, on organic net service revenue growth of 4% to 6% and adjusted EBITDA of $1.35 billion to $1.39 billion. Management guided to a 17.6% adjusted EBITDA margin, which would be an all-time high, and reaffirmed its target of a 20% segment adjusted operating margin by the end of fiscal 2028. The board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.34 per share, payable January 22, 2027.

Analysts responded constructively, with at least one broker lifting its price target to $86 from $65 while keeping a neutral stance. The offsetting negatives were real: revenue of $3.88 billion missed the roughly $4.1 billion consensus, GAAP fiscal 2027 EPS guidance of $5.65 to $5.90 fell short of estimates, and free cash flow of about $300 million will absorb roughly $500 million of CM-related cash outflows.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

The rally was overwhelmingly idiosyncratic. Infrastructure-focused funds and engineering peers were flat to modestly changed: [FLR](https://tickeron.com/ticker/FLR/) added about 0.7%, [J](https://tickeron.com/ticker/J/) was little changed, [KBR](https://tickeron.com/ticker/KBR/) slipped about 1%, and the S&P 500 was slightly lower. Nothing in the sector tape explains an 11% move.

Trading was active, with roughly 240,000 shares changing hands in the first half hour — a pace consistent with a heavier-than-average session for a stock that typically trades about 1.5 million shares a day — after substantial repositioning in Monday evening's after-hours session. Technically, the gap lifted the shares decisively above the $70–$73 ceiling that had capped every rally since August and extended a rebound that began at the October low, leaving the stock still well below where it traded a year ago.

# News Significance Score

The scale runs from 0, meaning no meaningful news and a move that is normal for the stock, to 100, meaning transformative news and an extreme, rare price move. AECOM's score is 63 out of 100. The verified news was solid but not transformative relative to a company of this size: a modest adjusted earnings beat, record margins and backlog, and in-line guidance, partly offset by a revenue miss. The price action, however, was highly unusual. The stock's average absolute daily move over the past 60 sessions is about 1.6%, and today's gain is roughly 7.5 times that. No session in that stretch came close to an 11.8% move; the largest was about 5.2%. Strong-but-not-exceptional news combined with a rare, outsized move produces the mid-60s score.

# What Comes Next for ACM

Attention shifts to execution. Fiscal 2027 first-quarter results are expected in early February 2027, and investors will want evidence that the 4% to 6% net service revenue growth guidance is materializing as the CM business ramps in the second half. Delivery of the second construction management project near the end of fiscal 2027's second quarter is the key de-risking milestone, and any slippage would likely be punished quickly given the recent history. Free cash flow conversion, the roughly $500 million of CM cash outflows, and the January 6 record date for the higher dividend are also in focus. Risks include Middle East conflict exposure, slower awards in Americas transportation, and the gap between adjusted and GAAP earnings.
